solutions.check: 29 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Get into the armed forces and put the pieces back together?

blocks.note: first meaning: to enlist as a soldier
second meaning: to connect separate parts again

explanation.surface: A recruit hoping the army will make them whole again.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both enlisting in the military and literally reconnecting broken parts.

clue.text: Maxwell's end involved e.g. yacht – "pre-entrance to God's house"

indicators.note: a name's end is its final letter, so only the last letter of the surname is kept
involved suggests tangled up, so the letters that follow are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: last letter of the surname Maxwell
the letters of these words, rearranged

explanation.surface: Recalls Robert Maxwell, the press baron who died falling from his yacht, with a mock-pious epitaph.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Maxwell, the newspaper owner, met his end off his yacht in 1991, so the surface reads as a jibe about where he went next.
explanation.definitionFit: A lychgate is the roofed gateway into a churchyard, standing before the church door.

clue.text: Kate to Wills: "Get pickled, taking Philip's lead"

indicators.note: a name's lead is its opening letter, so just the first letter is wanted
taking means grabbing hold of something, so one word takes another inside it

blocks.note: to souse is to pickle or steep in brine, also slang for getting drunk
the first letter of Philip

explanation.surface: The Duchess urging Prince William to get drunk like his grandfather Prince Philip.
explanation.definitionFit: Kate Middleton is Prince William's wife, so what she is to him is his marriage partner.

clue.text: Warning: pressure by sexual partner that's done to get you worked up

definitions.text: that's done to get you worked up

blocks.note: the warning shout of a golfer
P is the physics symbol for pressure
slang for someone you sleep with

explanation.surface: A caution about being pushed by a lover into something meant to arouse you.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreplay is the sexual stimulation that comes before intercourse, intended to arouse.

clue.text: Balls up, luvvie-style? Get going!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: Ed Balls, the Labour politician
theatrical and affected, in the manner of a luvvie (a gushing actor)

explanation.surface: A mock-theatrical shout of dismay at a cock-up, ordering someone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls up' reads as the British slang for a botch; here Balls is the shadow minister Ed Balls, turned upwards. A luvvie is a gushing, affected actor.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly, so as a command it means clear off.

clue.text: Liberal, oily MPs accepting "Clegg's leader" – another opportunity for a British fiasco?

definitions.text: another opportunity for a British fiasco

indicators.note: liberal means free with things, so the letters are treated freely and rearranged
a name's leader is its front letter, so only the first is taken
accepting means taking in, so the rearranged letters admit another inside

blocks.note: the letters of these words, rearranged
first letter of Nick Clegg, Liberal Democrat leader

explanation.surface: A sneer at greasy Lib Dem politicians backing their leader before London hosts the Games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like a party label beside Clegg, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The 2012 Olympic Games in London were, in the satirist's eyes, a fresh chance for national embarrassment.

clue.text: "Calm down!" – Cameron's initial agitating of 'fool'

indicators.note: an initial is the opening letter of a name, so only that one is taken
agitating means shaking up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: first letter of Cameron
these two words' letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: Recalls David Cameron's 'Calm down, dear' jibe, provoking a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: To cool off is to calm down after anger, so the imperative matches the exclamation.

clue.text: One affected when Europe's wrecked (Greece finally having gone)

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the country's name
something that has gone is no longer there, so that letter is removed
something wrecked is smashed up, so the letters are broken and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
last letter of Greece

explanation.surface: Comment on the eurozone crisis, with Europe ruined and Greece crashing out.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one E from the letters of EUROPES, leaving EUROPS, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A poseur is someone with affected, pretentious manners, putting on airs.

clue.text: Posh cars, coarsened birds

blocks.note: first meaning: casual short form for Rolls-Royces
second meaning: a family of brightly coloured birds; coarsened hints at slang shortening

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are informal: Rollers for Rolls-Royce cars, and the roller is also a real bird, its name roughened from the full form.
explanation.definitionFit: Roller names both a luxury Rolls-Royce car in slang and a family of crow-sized, colourful birds.

clue.text: see 26ac.
Ex-leader putting her bust into naff, unprepossessing tops

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters are smashed and rebuilt in a new order
putting something into another places it inside
the tops of words are their first letters

blocks.note: first letter of naff
the word her, rearranged
first letter of unprepossessing

explanation.surface: A woman squeezing her bosom into unflattering, tacky tops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' and 'tops' both look like clothing talk; one rearranges, the other takes first letters. Naff is British slang for tacky.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first prime minister, a former national leader.

clue.text: Alert to new ideas? Not he, sadly – maybe Ed just needs to get end away

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are put in a disordered arrangement
getting the end away means the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: these letters, rearranged
Ed Balls, the Labour politician, is an example of an Ed
surface padding linking the Ed to the instruction that follows

explanation.surface: Bemoaning Ed Balls' lack of fresh ideas, with a smutty hint that he just needs sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get one's end away' is British slang for having sex; here it simply strips the last letter from BALLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the ball means being quick, sharp and aware, receptive to what is happening.

clue.text: Personal problem after lay that merely makes you feel better

definitions.text: that merely makes you feel better

indicators.note: after says the personal problem is placed behind the word for lay, not before it

blocks.note: to lay something is to place it
BO, body odour, is a personal hygiene problem

explanation.surface: Body odour following a one-night stand, and a remedy that only works in the mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' tempts as the sexual noun, as in 4 down; here it is the verb place.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy treatment with no active drug, helping only through the patient's belief.

clue.text: Return of disease – Dicky Rees guards genital area

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for unsound or shaky, so the letters are jumbled
guarding something means surrounding it protectively, so one part goes inside another

blocks.note: the name Rees, rearranged
the lap is the front of the lower body when seated

explanation.surface: A man called Rees protecting his crotch, alongside a disease coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is when a patient's illness returns after apparent recovery.

clue.text: "Verify any tweet put out by Sun!": that's Ian's term, as editor

indicators.note: put out means upset and disturbed, so the letters are disarranged

blocks.note: taken as written
S abbreviates Sunday, or sun

explanation.surface: A tabloid instruction to check Twitter stories, aimed at the Sun newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is the British tabloid in the surface, but supplies only S here. Ian Hislop became Private Eye's editor in 1986, so this issue marks his quarter century.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Hislop's tenure as editor of Private Eye had run a quarter of a century by 2011.

clue.text: (& 21dn.) Victoria certainly wasn't given the old trout treatment by gay?

blocks.note: trout can be caught by gently stroking them underwater, an old poaching method
pink is associated with gay culture, as in the pink pound

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria pointedly not being amused by a gay man's crude groping.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Victoria is famous for 'We are not amused'. 'Old trout' looks like an insult to her, but refers to the fish and tickling them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tickled pink means being greatly amused or delighted, the opposite of Victoria's famous frostiness.

clue.text: One who, in the past, appreciated a nice rack?

definitions.text: One who, in the past, appreciated a nice rack?

blocks.note: surface reading: a man ogling a woman's bosom, rack being slang for breasts
setter's reading: someone in history who made good use of the rack, the stretching device

explanation.walkthrough: The rack was an instrument for stretching victims in old interrogations; the slang sense of breasts is the decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: An interrogator of old would value a good rack, the device used to inflict pain.

clue.text: Instruction to one who plays with sex aid endlessly ...

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: a vibrator is a sex toy

explanation.surface: Smutty direction to someone playing with a sex toy that never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One who plays' reads as someone playing with themselves; it is a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Vibrato is a musical direction to a performer to make the note pulse slightly in pitch.

clue.text: 'Patronage' means one American getting shafted by Ginger?

indicators.note: being shafted means being done over, so the letters are wrecked and rearranged

blocks.note: a, meaning one
abbreviation for the United States
ginger is a spice

explanation.surface: An American being cheated by a redhead, with patronage the theme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ginger' looks like a redhead (or Ginger Spice); it is just the spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Under someone's auspices means with their support or sponsorship.

clue.text: Whitewash balls inside part of bra

indicators.note: inside places one part within another

blocks.note: a bra has two cups
in cricket an over is a set of six balls

explanation.surface: Something stuffed inside a bra cup to cover up.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled by one bowler; 'balls' looks bawdy.
explanation.definitionFit: A whitewash is a concealment of wrongdoing, the same thing as a cover-up.

clue.text: Testicles at first stored in glass bottles – very important for a body

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter only
stored in means placed inside a holder

blocks.note: vials are small glass bottles
first letter of testicles

explanation.surface: Testicles preserved in jars, as in a medical museum.
explanation.definitionFit: The vitals are the essential organs, such as heart and lungs, that the body cannot survive without.

clue.text: see 15dn.
Maybe Rupert's on the booze (keeps cheerful)

blocks.note: Rupert Bear, the British children's cartoon character, is a bear
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Rupert Murdoch hitting the bottle under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: Rupert looks like Murdoch, beleaguered over phone hacking; he is Rupert Bear, a children's comic-strip bear.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear up is to stay brave and cheerful under strain.

clue.text: After one, seniors start missing things growing big

indicators.note: a start that is missing means the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: a, meaning one
elders are older people

explanation.surface: Older people, one by one, forgetting things, while something grows.
explanation.definitionFit: Alders are trees, which are things that grow to a large size.

clue.text: Talk about sick punchline!

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to yap is to chatter
feeling off means unwell

explanation.surface: Discussing a joke in poor taste.
explanation.definitionFit: The payoff of a joke is its climax, the line that delivers the laugh.

clue.text: State of endless bad odour in Italian corruption

indicators.note: endless means without an ending, so the last letter goes
corruption is a spoiling, so the letters are disordered
in places one part within another

blocks.note: the letters of Italian, rearranged
a hum is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: Italian politics smelling of corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a condition; it is a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithuania is a Baltic country, a sovereign nation.

clue.text: (& 10dn.) Cheap rag makes a cleaner energy source

blocks.note: a daily is a British term for a domestic cleaner who comes in every day
a star, like the sun, is a source of energy

explanation.surface: A cheap cloth that turns into a greener, cleaner power supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheap rag' seems a duster beside 'cleaner'; it is a tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daily Star is a downmarket British tabloid newspaper, and rag is slang for a paper.

clue.text: LibDem-Conservative leaders in "partnership performance" – how sweet!

indicators.note: leaders of words are their first letters
in places one part within another

blocks.note: a duet is a performance by two
first letters of LibDem and Conservative

explanation.surface: Mocking the coalition as a cosy double act.
explanation.walkthrough: The 2010 UK coalition joined the Liberal Democrats and the Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Dulcet means sweet and soothing, usually of sounds.

clue.text: Don't feel this if you're rough

definitions.text: Don't feel this if you're rough

blocks.note: surface reading: avoid touching something if you are clumsy
setter's reading: rough means unwell, and an unwell person says they are not feeling quite themselves

explanation.walkthrough: In British usage feeling rough means feeling ill, and the idiom is 'not feeling yourself'.
explanation.definitionFit: The reflexive pronoun completes the idiom about being off-colour or unwell.
